key_facts: The Eurospeech paper was accepted and will be presented in Aalborg, Denmark, in September.
PhD C discussed experiments on online normalization, including varying time constants and using different means for silence and speech, but found no significant improvement.
Adding white noise at a level 15 dB below the peak energy of utterances resulted in smoother MFCC features without worsening speech recognition performance.
PhD C mentioned that the LDA filter derived from clean speech improved recognition rates on TI-Digits compared to the one from noisy speech.
Grad A plans to conduct experiments on phone recognition using TIMIT, incorporating knowledge of voicing to improve results.
Grad G encountered issues with Wiener filtering, suspecting a bug in the implementation, and considered using a modified approach from Carlos' thesis.
PhD E is working on VTS (Vectorial Taylor Series) for noise removal, using a single Gaussian for noise estimation and a codebook for clean speech.
PhD E's experiments with VTS showed that using only the first ten frames for noise estimation did not yield significant improvements.
Professor B suggested using known nonspeech sections for noise estimation to better isolate the effects of different methods.
PhD E mentioned that the dimensionality of the Gaussian used for noise estimation is 23, resulting in 40 numbers for each frame.
